name: Assassin
rule: Call the name of another character. When the killed character is called to take its turn, it must remain silent and skip its entire turn for this round without revealing its card.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Witch
windows: You open the `choose-character` window and the `witch-takeover` window.
rule: Gather resources, then call the name of another character to bewitch; your turn is put on hold and you cannot build. When the bewitched character is called, its owner gathers resources and their turn immediately ends (no build, no character ability). You then resume your turn as if you were playing the bewitched character: you use that character's abilities and build limit, with YOUR hand, YOUR gold, and YOUR city. If the bewitched character is not in play this round, you do not resume.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Magistrate
rule: Assign three warrant markers facedown to three different characters; one is the signed warrant, the target. If the targeted player pays to build a district during their turn, you may reveal the warrant and confiscate that district, building it in your city for free. The confiscated district counts toward the target's building limit and the target gets their gold back. You may confiscate only the first district the target pays to build, and only if you do not already have an identical district.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Thief
windows: You open the `choose-character` window and the `thief-rob` window.
rule: Call the name of another character. When a player reveals that character to take its turn, you immediately take all of that player's gold. You cannot rob a rank 1 character, the killed character, or the bewitched character.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Spy
rule: Choose another player and name a district type. Look at that player's hand. For each card of the named type, take 1 gold from that player and gain 1 card from the deck. If the player has fewer gold than matching cards, take all their gold and still gain a card per matching card.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Blackmailer
rule: Assign two threat markers facedown to two different characters; one shows the flowered lace and is the target. When a threatened player is called, they must gather resources, then resolve the threat: they may bribe you by giving half their gold rounded down (a player with 1 gold gives 0), removing their marker; or refuse. If they refuse you may reveal their marker; revealing the flowered lace takes all their gold. A threatened player must resolve the threat before using abilities or building. You cannot threaten a rank 1 character, the killed character, or the bewitched character.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Magician
rule: Choose one: exchange your entire hand with another player's hand (if you have zero cards you simply take theirs), or discard any number of cards from your hand to the bottom of the deck and draw an equal number.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Wizard
rule: Look at another player's hand and choose one card. Either pay to build it immediately (it does not count toward your building limit) or add it to your hand. During this turn you may build districts identical to districts already in your city.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Seer
rule: Take a card at random from each other player's hand and add them to your hand, then give one card from your hand to each player you took from. A player with no cards is skipped. Your building limit this turn is two.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: King
windows: No window: take the crown in your effect.
rule: Gain 1 gold per noble district in your city. At some point during your turn you must take the crown. If killed, at end of round reveal the King and take the crown as heir. If bewitched, you still take the crown.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Emperor
rule: Gain 1 gold per noble district in your city. You must take the crown from its holder and give it to a different player, not yourself, then take either 1 gold or 1 random card from that player's stash or hand. If killed, at end of round take the crown and pass it to a different player, taking nothing. Not usable in 2-player games.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

name: Patrician
windows: No window: take the crown in your effect.
rule: Gain 1 CARD per noble district in your city. At some point during your turn you must take the crown. If killed, at end of round reveal the Patrician and take the crown as heir. If bewitched, you still take the crown.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.

rule: Gain 1 gold per religious district in your city. During this round the rank 8 character cannot use its ability on your districts. If killed, rank 8 may target you; if bewitched, rank 8 cannot target the Witch's districts but can target the Bishop's.

name: Abbot
rule: Gain either 1 gold or 1 card per religious district in your city, in any combination you declare before taking. If at any point during your turn you are not the richest player, the richest player must give you 1 gold; on a tie you choose which tied player pays, and if you are among the tied you receive nothing.

rule: Gain 1 CARD per religious district in your city. When you build a district and lack the gold, you may take the shortfall from one player, giving that player one card from your hand per gold taken. The player cannot refuse and you cannot take more than needed.

windows: No window: refund at end of turn.
rule: At the end of your turn, take back all the gold you paid to build districts this turn, but not gold paid for other reasons such as the Smithy or the Tax Collector. You can only build what you could afford at the time.

name: Warlord
rule: Gain 1 gold per military district in your city. You may destroy one district of your choice, yours or a rival's, by paying one fewer gold than its cost. You cannot destroy a district in a completed city. Destroyed districts go to the bottom of the deck.

You cannot take from a completed city, nor take a district identical to one you already have, and the district you give must not be identical to one they already have.

name: Tax Collector
rule: While the Tax Collector is in the game, immediately after any player builds a district they place one gold from their stash on the Tax Collector's token, even if they did not pay to build it. A player with no gold left after building pays nothing, and the Tax Collector pays no tax. At any time during your turn you may take all gold from the token. The tax is charged even in rounds where the Tax Collector is not in play, and leftover gold carries over. In 2-3 player games a player holding the Tax Collector still pays tax for their other character.
tests:
- one test per clause above; name each after the clause it proves.
- at least one test that would FAIL if the ability were a no-op.
